newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai police charge two with negligence in fire.
newsitem.headline: Thai police charge two with negligence in fire.

text.p: Thai police have charged two men with negligence causing death in connection with the country's deadliest-ever hotel fire last week that killed 90 people, police said on Thursday.
The managing director of the Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel, Thavorn Ujjin, was also charged with illegal modification of the building, police said.

Thavorn and Chamnien Sudto, an employee in the hotel's restaurant, were both charged and interrogated for their complicity in the fire in the resort town of Pattaya, about 200 km (120 miles) southeast of Bangkok.
Others were being interrogated but no one else had yet been charged, police said.
Thavorn, who is suffering from heart problems, was released on two million baht ($66,667) bail on Wednesday night. Chamnien was still being held as no one had come to bail him out, police said.

The maximum penalty for negligence causing death is 10 years in prison and a 20,000 baht fine. The penalty for illegal modification of a building is five years in prison and a 200,000 baht fine, police said.
The 400-room, 16-storey hotel was gutted in a six-hour fire last Friday after a gas explosion in the lobby-level restaurant sparked a blaze which then spread to other levels.
Rescue workers said the high death toll was due to insufficient fire-prevention equipment, a lack of sprinklers and alarms and the fact that fire exit doors were locked.
Officials had said the hotel locked the doors to prevent guests from leaving without paying their bills.
The fire was the second major disaster in recent years in which blocked emergency exits trapped dozens of victims.
About 200 teenage workers perished in May 1993 after a fire broke out inside a locked warehouse at Kader Industrial toy factory in Nakhon Pathom province just north of Bangkok. ($1 = 30 baht)
